churn_resistance.rationale: Every boundary is typed and every concern lives in one well-named module: raw API access in api-client, view-model construction in loaders, page data in PageData, page title in a TitleStrategy. Adding a page touches routes + loaders + one component; a framework upgrade would ripple almost nowhere. The bespoke scroll logic and the /_data protocol are the main custom surface, but both are isolated and documented.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared runtime dependency but is never imported; the app deliberately uses native form elements.
withEventReplay() is redundant on Angular 22: since v22 provideClientHydration() enables incremental hydration by default, which includes event replay (angular.dev PR #71120, hydration guide).
findings.suggestion: Call provideClientHydration() with no arguments (or keep it only while supporting v21), so future deprecations of the feature flag don't bite.

findings.issue: allowedHosts: ['*'] disables Angular SSR's host validation; the SSR guidance recommends an explicit list unless a trusted proxy validates forwarded headers.
findings.suggestion: Keep the reasoning in the comment, but prefer an explicit allowedHosts list (or trustProxyHeaders) once the production host is known.

findings.issue: Scroll restoration is hand-rolled on top of Router Scroll events with in-memory scrolling fully disabled, duplicating what withInMemoryScrolling provides and depending on Scroll event ordering.
findings.suggestion: Consider the router's built-in anchorScrolling/scrollPositionRestoration with a custom RouterScroller only for the query-only case, to reduce custom router-internals coupling.

findings.issue: A module-level promise cache lives in the server bundle and is shared across requests; safe here (public snapshot data, 60 s TTL) but a foot-gun if per-user data is ever introduced.
findings.suggestion: Document the public-data assumption on the cache, or key entries by request context if the API ever serves user-specific data.

findings.issue: The debounce + linkedSignal + pushedQ bookkeeping is a subtle three-piece state machine for 'follow the URL except while typing'.
findings.suggestion: Simplify by deriving the input value from a signal set on (input) and reconciled against the URL in an effect, or add a comment-level note that this is intentional to avoid fighting the URL round-trip.

findings.issue: The custom /_data endpoint plus TransferState key management is bespoke plumbing that Angular's transfer cache / resource() would provide for free (at the cost of larger payloads).
findings.suggestion: Keep it (the payload win is real and it's well documented in README), but revisit when Angular's stable resource/httpResource covers the same use case with less custom protocol.

summary: This is a showcase of current Angular: v22.2, zoneless by default, stable @Service, linkedSignal, signal inputs, control-flow templates, provideAppInitializer, RESPONSE_INIT, and route resolvers bound straight to component inputs, with the Angular skill docs confirming each choice. The architecture is unusually churn-resistant — all PokeAPI access and raw shapes are confined to one server module behind typed view models, and the one custom piece (scroll handling) is isolated in the root component. The only real deductions are a dead @angular/forms dependency, a now-redundant withEventReplay(), and a wildcard allowedHosts that the SSR guidance cautions against.

apis.replacement: No-op since v22: provideClientHydration() enables incremental hydration (incl. event replay) by default; the flag is redundant but not deprecated
Still the documented, stable data-loading pattern; resource()/router resources are the emerging alternative (router resources are developer preview in v22)
